questions.q: Which table stores supplier invoice headers, and what is its primary key?
questions.explain: AP_INVOICES_ALL stores one row per supplier invoice, with INVOICE_ID as its primary key.

questions.q: How does an invoice header connect back to its supplier?
options: Through a PARTY_ID column directly on AP_INVOICES_ALL
Through a VENDOR_ID column on AP_INVOICES_ALL, which ties to POZ_SUPPLIERS
Invoices do not reference suppliers at all
Through the invoice line table only
questions.explain: AP_INVOICES_ALL carries a VENDOR_ID column pointing to the supplier record in POZ_SUPPLIERS.

questions.q: What is the composite primary key of AP_INVOICE_LINES_ALL?
questions.explain: AP_INVOICE_LINES_ALL is keyed by the combination of INVOICE_ID and LINE_NUMBER, reflecting its parent/child relationship to the invoice header.

questions.q: Why are invoice lines and invoice distributions NOT the same thing?
options: They are the same thing, just named differently
A single invoice line can be split across multiple accounting distributions, so the distribution table captures a finer level of detail than the line
Distributions only exist for customer transactions, not supplier invoices
Lines always have exactly one distribution, with no exceptions
questions.explain: A single line's amount can be split across multiple distributions, each potentially posting to a different account — that split is what AP_INVOICE_DISTRIBUTIONS_ALL stores.

questions.q: Which table's rows ultimately feed into Subledger Accounting on an invoice's way to the General Ledger?
questions.explain: It is the distribution rows — the accounting-level detail beneath the lines — that feed Subledger Accounting (XLA_) on the way to GL.
